(2) The field table's id, population, _seed and version-stamp rows read 'none — a required key' (l.627-632), and V08 §3.5 step 3 refuses empty or unreadable values, against item 125 (b) ('a missing or empty field never refuses') and R2-40 (3). required_change: As verify-vol-V07-V08-r2t's G125-V08 words it. Clause (1), one fix with VCS-r2-02: the dossier's own shape and stamps select the adapter in every case (bound line, single accepting adapter, at creation the newest line noted line_defaulted); HostContext.line is checked, never chosen from (an unsupported or contradicting line refuses E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED; a differing accepted line leaves the selection standing, both lines reported); B19, T-V8-11 and T-V8-61 (b) follow, and a J-V8 row records it. also_reported.claim: Persists from round 1 in two parts; the rest of G125-V08 is fixed (the fallback column, `field_fallback`, `presentWeek`, `week`/`realm`/`customLibrary` retired at every site, the final-check brief, T-V8-61). (1) Clause (4), fixed against the owner's bar. V08 §2.4's *Selection* tries `HostContext.line` first and says 'only where two registered lines accept one dossier … does `line` decide which line's reading builds it (B19)'. T-V8-11 likewise: 'HostContext.line picks when given'. So in that case one dossier makes a different document with and without a host context. That contradicts item 125 (e) ('the same dossier with and without a host context yields the identical document and hash'), R2-40 (2) (`line` is among the fields 'none able to change a document a dossier makes'), V08's own J-V8.130 ('a host input must never change a map a dossier makes (T125-2)') and V08 §3.17's one-input row ('a host context present and absent give the identical document and hash'). T-V8-61 (b) tests T125-2 only with `line` the pinned line. Same defect as verify-scope-r2t VCS-r2-02. (2) Clause (2) and R2-40 (3) ('every field has its standalone fallback, reported'), against item 125 (b) ('a missing or empty field never refuses'). The field table's `id`, `population`, `_seed` and `schemaVersion`/`generatorVersion`/`simulationVersion` rows read 'none — a required key', and §3.5 step 3 refuses with `E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE` an empty or non-integer `population`, a malformed `id`, a non-array `institutions` and a non-string `name` or `tier`. Yet §2.4's own lead says the fallback 'serves an empty or unreadable value', and J-V8.130 says 'the generator already has a standalone choice for every field'. T-V8-61 (a) empties only 'every empty-able value'.
also_reported.required_change: (1) ONE FIX with VCS-r2-02, as it words it. V08 §2.4's *Selection*: the dossier's own shape and stamps select the adapter in every case — (1) the document's bound line when its adapter accepts, (2) the single registered adapter that accepts, (3) at a creation with several accepting, the newest registered line, recorded and noted `line_defaulted`. `HostContext.line` is checked, never chosen from: a named line no adapter supports, or one the dossier's stamps contradict, refuses `E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED` (B5); a named line that is registered and accepts but differs from the selection leaves the selection standing, the report naming both lines. Replace 'only where two registered lines accept one dossier … does `line` decide which line's reading builds it (B19), SettlementForge's own statement of its line, reported' by 'with several registered lines accepting one dossier the dossier's own selection still decides, so one dossier makes the same document and hash with and without a host context (item 125 (e); T125-2)'. B19 reads 'two registered adapters accept a new settlement's dossier, a line named or not'. T-V8-11's two-adapter clause: 'the same document and hash with `HostContext.line` naming either line and with none'. T-V8-61 (b) adds that two-adapter fixture. In §3.16 (9) (a) and J-V8.130, '`line` (which picks the adapter, V08 §2.4)' / '`line` stays the one host field, picking the adapter' read '`line`, which the selection checks (V08 §2.4)'. (2) The `population` row's fallback: empty, non-integer or outside [0, 10⁷] → the population at the midpoint of the tier word's rung range (DR23), else the blueprint's default population, noted `field_fallback`. The `_seed` row: empty or unreadable → H32 of the settlement key, noted. The `institutions` row: not an array → read as absent (S2's roster, as standalone), noted. Delete those three cases, and a non-string `name` or `tier` (their rows' fallbacks), from §3.5 step 3's refusal list. For `id` and the three version stamps — the line's identity, which `recognise` and the key law read — add one J-V8 row recording why an unreadable value is no dossier of the line (B3, B5) under item 125 (b), and cite it in their fallback cells. T-V8-61 (a) adds a fixture with `population` empty and `_seed` empty that generates a full map, each noted.

claim: V11's repair handed V08 the rule 'a stressor and the condition it was promoted into draw one look' (repair-r2-V11.md HAND-OFFS, l.169-171); no unit states it. V08 §3.11 (l.2050-2064) and §3.5 step 3 (l.1627-1628) put each stressor as its own overlay cond:stress:<type> beside the conditions' cond:<id> overlays, and V08 §3.16 (7) (b) gives each overlay its own map row. V11 §3.25.9 maps both the under_siege stressor and the war_pressure archetype to siege (item 122 (b): 'war_pressure with a siege, the siege stressor'), plague_onset and plague to quarantine, and mass_migration and regional_migration_pressure to refugeeCamp. §10.2 Crisis looks (a), (d), (e) and DR44 draw each standing overlay's look, and no rule merges two overlays of one crisis. A siege reported both as a stressor and as a condition therefore draws two siege looks, each with camps sized by its own severity: the camped ground doubles against item 122 (c)'s 'the scale follows severity and tier', and two 'Siege camps' lines appear on the card, in Find's crises section, in the legend and in V10's look read. V08's edge row (l.2632) covers only 'a stressor listed twice is one overlay'.
required_change: V08 §3.16 (7) (b) adds the pairing rule: state how the digest recognises a stressor and the condition SettlementForge promoted it into (the condition whose archetype is the stressor's type, or whose triggeredAt names the stressor, as SF0's census confirms). While both stand, the pair draws ONE look — the condition's, with its name, weeks and forces. The stressor's overlay draws none, and its look resumes if the condition ends while the stressor is still listed. DR44's source clause cites the rule; V08 §3.17's crisis row adds the edge; T-V8-59 gains a stressor-and-condition pair that draws one siege.

Only V11's `crisis.map` row `event` · `calamity` → `disaster` maps to it (V11 l. 4560), and V11 adds 'Every calamity draws `disaster`' (l. 4568–4569). V08 §3.16 (7) (b) (l. 2496–2499) and V08 §2.5's digest field (l. 731) set `event` only from `triggeredAt.sourceEventType` when the crisis census lists the word, and the census's crisis events are `PLAGUE`, `REFUGEE_WAVE` and `RAID_OR_MONSTER_ATTACK` (l. 2492–2493).
